titles: L'Espace vide: Écrits sur le théâtre
Tragédie classique et théâtre du XIXe siècle
partial: Histoire de la littérature prolétarienne en France
notes: Landscape, straight-on, a second-hand bookstall (Paris) in low afternoon sun with strong side light and shadow bands; nearly every book is in a plastic sleeve, so there are reflections. French throughout. Most books stand face-out (Gallimard nrf covers), so the titles come from covers rather than spines; the Mishima trilogy, Carnets, L'Emploi du temps and the Éditions de Minuit spines are in stacks read sideways or upside down. Series volumes: Journal II (Léon Bloy) and Correspondance I (Morand/Chardonne) are labelled by the volume as printed. Les Meilleures is a Filipacchi humour collection ('les 200 plus drôles histoires drôles de Lui') rather than a novel, but it is a book with a printed title. Partial: the two far-left spines cut by the frame (Essai général de stratégie, Histoire de la littérature prolétarienne en France, series name only partly visible), Le Chat et le Diable (Joyce, lower half of the cover hidden), L'Écrivain des ombres (Philip Roth, right edge hidden), Les Gommes (faint Minuit spine in the stack), Un an and Jérôme Lindon (Jean Echenoz spines at the top of the stack, small type), Léo Ferré (black spine, probably a monograph, only the name reads). Left out: the wrapped books in the lower half whose only marking is a handwritten author name on the sleeve (Aragon, Abellio, Leiris, Kessel, Mistral, Loti, G. Mathieu, Ph. Muray, Hugnet, Jouvet, Eliade, Dos Passos, Cortázar), the two 'Œuvres complètes' volumes with no readable author, the Boris Vian and Pierre Hebey spines (author only), the book marked 'Lettres' in script (no author), the remaining Minuit spines at the top right (Claude Simon and others, titles too small), and the stacked books seen edge-on. The Léon Daudet and Léon Bloy covers carry portrait photographs of the authors.
